slides.title: Weak References & Cycle Breaking
slides.prompt: std::weak_ptr holds a non-owning ('weak') reference to an object managed by std::shared_ptr. It is used to break cyclic reference memory leaks and inspect object availability without incrementing use count.

slides.title: Locking weak_ptr
slides.prompt: Fill in the member function that converts a std::weak_ptr into a std::shared_ptr to access the object safely.

slides.title: Cyclic Reference Problem
slides.prompt: What memory defect occurs when two std::shared_ptr instances store shared_ptr references pointing directly to each other?
options: Memory leak: Reference counts never drop to zero, so neither object is destroyed
slides.correctAnswer: Memory leak: Reference counts never drop to zero, so neither object is destroyed

slides.title: Checking Expiration
slides.prompt: Fill in the member function that returns true if the referenced object has already been destroyed.

slides.title: weak_ptr Dereferencing
slides.prompt: Why can you not dereference a std::weak_ptr directly using operator* or operator->?
options: Because the underlying object might have been deleted asynchronously; it must be converted to shared_ptr first via lock()
Because std::weak_ptr does not store memory address location
Because weak_ptr is designed for integer values only
slides.correctAnswer: Because the underlying object might have been deleted asynchronously; it must be converted to shared_ptr first via lock()

slides.title: Weak Reference Counter
slides.prompt: Fill in the pointer type used in class structures for parent pointers to prevent cycles with children.

slides.title: Control Block Lifetime with weak_ptr
slides.prompt: When is the Control Block freed if all std::shared_ptrs are destroyed, but std::weak_ptrs still exist?
options: The managed object is destroyed immediately, but the Control Block remains until all weak_ptrs are destroyed
Both object and control block are destroyed immediately
The managed object remains alive until weak_ptrs are cleared
slides.correctAnswer: The managed object is destroyed immediately, but the Control Block remains until all weak_ptrs are destroyed

slides.title: Constructing weak_ptr from shared_ptr
slides.prompt: Fill in the type used to initialize a weak pointer from a shared pointer variable 'sp'.

slides.title: std::enable_shared_from_this Purpose
options: Allows a class member method to safely create a valid std::shared_ptr to 'this' without creating duplicate control blocks
Enables automatic conversion from raw pointers to weak pointers
Protects class member variables with internal mutex locks
slides.correctAnswer: Allows a class member method to safely create a valid std::shared_ptr to 'this' without creating duplicate control blocks
